SECTION II Curricular Matters Which Require Confirmation by the Faculty Senate PROGRAM CHANGES: COLLEGE OF HEALTH SCIENCES: Human Development and Family Science-BS See Appendix A In the Spring of 2020, Human Development and Family Science made a number of changes to the structure of the HDF curriculum.
Recently, however, we noticed that the legislation (19-20-28B) that was put forth and approved for the changes to the HDF major were not exactly what the department intended.
Although ecampus accurately reflects what was stated in the legislation, the changes do not line up with our intended changes.
Change Requested: HDF is seeking to reconfigure the subplans so that students in 2020 catalog year and forward will use the new subplans.
Students using the 2019 and earlier catalog year will complete old subplans.

Both the new and old subplans must be present simultaneously to allow this to happen.
Health Studies-BS See Appendix B We are proposing that HLT312: Intersecting Social Identities and Health be approved as a specialization class for all three specialization areas: global & environmental health, health promotion, and health services.
The 3 credit class examines how social identities, social roles, and social categories (i.e., race, class, gender, sexuality, ability, age, etc.) affect health from an interdisciplinary perspective.
We believe that students in all three specializations who are interested in this topic would benefit from the class.
COLLEGE OF THE ENVIRONMENT AND LIFE SCIENCES: Marine Affairs Department See Appendix C Marine Affairs - BA & BS majors: EGR 213G was recently cross-listed with MAF (Fac Sen #19-20-28A).
The course is co-taught by professors in Ocean Engineering, Marine Affairs, and GSO.
EGR/MAF 213G introduces students to the fundamental concepts of energy with regard to the physical, environmental, and socioeconomic aspects, which prepares them to critically understand global energy challenges and possible solutions 1

for sustainable energy development. We are requesting that MAF 213G be added to the coastal and marine policy and management concentration list for Marine Affairs BS and BA majors. COLLEGE OF BUSINESS: Core Requirements for Majors Listed: See Appendix D The college of business is requesting to remove the language requirement of two semesters that is currently required to complete the BSBA degree for all Accounting, Finance, Marketing, Supply Chain Management, Management, Management Information Systems*, and Innovation & Entrepreneurship majors. The replacement will be two semesters of a Global Cultural Experience requirement. Given the global nature of all of our business courses, the foreign language requirement is no longer necessary to achieve global competency. Management: See Appendix E The Management major requirements are being updated (see attached) to 1) differentiate the major from the new Entrepreneurship and Innovation Major and 2) allow for greater flexibility and customization of the degree for students to study different facets of management (human resources, sustainability, globalization, etc.) and be better prepared for the job market. 2

Business Analytics and Intelligence (BAI) is the area of study that deals with skills, technologies, practices for efficient data management, continuous iterative exploration and investigation of business performance to gain insight and drive business planning.
There are an increasing number of BAI tools and methodologies newly introduced to the industry and academia every day.

These tools and methodologies provide field practitioners with statistical and operations analysis, the formation of predictive models, application of optimization techniques, and the communication of these results to customers, business partners, and college executives.
Business Analytics and Intelligence requires quantitative methods and evidence-based data for business modeling and decision making.
Business Analytics and Intelligence provide the industry with a great deal of benefits.
Data management solutions and analytical software continue to proliferate and provide better decision-making tools.
Businesses are increasingly relying on business analytics to gain a competitive advantage or just to keep up with the competition.
As such, students trained with BAI programs are highly-demanding future employees.
According to the U.S.
Bureau of Labor Statistics, Data scientist salaries in the United

States: $130,290 (2017), and Data scientist was ranked at #1 among 50 best jobs in America (Glassdoor.com).
Business analysts often specialize in a particular industry, such as medical science, telecommunications and energy.
Or, they may work in a specific area of business, like marketing, human resources or supply chain management.
In particular, those who are working for smaller firms may serve as general practitioners.
In all settings, the job of these professionals is to define a problem, collect and analyze data pertaining to it, evaluate company processes and procedures, and ultimately recommend and deploy strategies designed to solve the issue.
The Business Analytics and Intelligence program is to provide students with the opportunity to better integrate data insights into their analyses and decision-making process.
The program is also designed to strengthen knowledge from their primary major with advanced business analytics skills.
Students will be prepared to bring insights from the large amounts of data to their functional areas such as marketing, finance, supply chain management, accounting among others.

Students will specialize in one of the functional areas of business to gain additional skills that will prepare them for data-driven and analytics-based decision making.
Many of the courses of the program will be revised to include the important learning goals specific to Business Analytics and Intelligence.
Some courses listed in the COB curriculum will be tailored for BAI students.

These courses were offered for the Management Information Systems (MIS) major in the college of business.
